provenance.instrument: 2011 Zoning Ordinance of the Borough of Wilson (Chapter 170 Zoning, Ord. No. 760 of 12-27-2012, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WI0763, Borough of Wilson, Northampton County (170-23 'Borough': 'The Borough of Wilson, located in Northampton County'). Each district article lists its by-right, special exception and conditional uses and its lot and yard figures as text. The Table of Use Regulations (170-82) and Table 2 of parking spaces (170-95A) are PDF attachments and were not opened. Floodplain rules are in 170-86A and Chapter 110. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 02-09-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' 170-22 carries Ord. No. 820 of 2-9-2026
checks: In-law suite: a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board in R-1, R-2 and TC (170-30H, 170-35J, 170-45O). 'One in-law suite to a residential dwelling shall be permitted, provided that the conditions set forth in this subsection are met' (170-83H(9)). A special exception needs a site plan certified by an engineer, surveyor, architect or landscape architect and Planning Commission review (170-11, 170-15)

The suite 'shall occupy no more than 25% of the total usable floor area of the principal residence, not including any garage', may have its own cooking, sleeping, living and bathroom facilities, and is limited to one per dwelling (170-83H(9)(a), (b), (e))

'In-law suites shall be part of the principal residence or may be contained in the existing accessory structure such as a garage. No new separate structures on the same lot with the principal residence shall be permitted to be constructed for this use' (170-83H(9)(c))

'The intent of these provisions is to allow for related family members to reside on the premises' (170-83H(9)). The section sets no family test of its own. Ask the zoning officer whether the Board will require relatives

The code's definition of an accessory dwelling unit, 'A separate second dwelling unit which may be located within a structure in which the principal use is for a single-family dwelling', allows it only if it has at most three rooms or 800 sq ft of livable area or 40% of the residential floor area (not counting basement and attic), whichever is less, is not meant for more than two people, stays in the same ownership as the house, and the owner lives in the principal unit (170-23 'Dwelling' H). No use list names an accessory dwelling unit. The in-law suite section sets its own full standards and lets a suite go in an existing garage, which the definition does not cover (170-83H(9)). So whether the definition binds an in-law suite is not settled, and the tool does not apply its 800 sq ft, two person, ownership or owner rules. Ask the zoning officer

Each in-law suite must be registered with the Borough Code Enforcement Officer, and the Northampton County Department of Human Services or another agency must certify that the wastewater facilities can serve the house and the suite (170-83H(9)(f), (g))

Parking: the house's required spaces 'plus one additional off-street parking space for the in-law suite' (170-83H(9)(d)). The house's own count is in Table 2, a PDF attachment that was not opened (170-95A). A code search snippet of that row gives the house '2 spaces per dwelling unit' followed by more words not shown, so the house count was not read in full. Spaces are at least 10 ft by 18 ft, paved, 5 ft from a street line and 2 ft from side and rear lines (170-95A, C(1), (3))

R-1 and R-2 list 'Average lot area per dwelling unit' of 6,000 and 5,000 sq ft for a single-family detached lot (170-32B, 170-37A(2)). Whether the in-law suite counts as a dwelling unit for this figure is not settled. The section calls the suite an 'accessory use', and in R-2 a whole two-family dwelling needs only 5,000 sq ft (2,500 sq ft per unit, 170-37C), so the tool does not count the suite against the figure

R-2 permits a two-family dwelling by right: two units 'entirely separated by vertical walls or horizontal floors', on 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide and 100 ft deep, with 2,500 sq ft per unit (170-34C, 170-37C, 170-83B(2)). The definition of a two-family detached dwelling names only units stacked over one another, each with its own entry (170-23 'Dwelling' E). Multifamily dwellings of three or more units are a special exception in R-2 and TC on 20,000 sq ft (170-35A, 170-45A, 170-83B(3))

TC lists no single-family or two-family dwelling, only an in-law suite and multifamily dwellings by special exception (170-44, 170-45). A house there is read as a nonconforming use, which may be enlarged by no more than 40% of its floor or ground area, with the parking the enlargement needs (170-92A)

Floodplain: 'All structures, with the exception of those specifically allowed in § 170-86A(4)' are prohibited in the floodplain, and new construction in the floodway is prohibited (170-86A(1)(i), (5)(b), (c)). 'No variance shall be granted for any of the prohibited uses or activities in § 170-86A(5) to locate in the floodplain' (170-86A(8)(b)[2]), and Chapter 110 yields to the more restrictive rule (110-2, 110-3). An addition to a house may instead be read as an improvement of an existing structure, which in the FF and FA areas needs full floodproofing at 10% or more of its market value (170-86A(6)(d)[1]). 'No improvement or reconstruction of an existing structure shall be allowed within any FW area' (170-86A(6)(a)), so even a suite inside the house is barred in the floodway. 'Within any identified floodplain area, unless a variance is requested and obtained, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' (110-22). An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have at most 200 sq ft (110-22E). Sewage disposal facilities are prohibited in the floodplain (170-86A(5)(m), 110-23). Every development there needs building and zoning permits regardless of value (170-86A(7)(a)). The Zoning Hearing Board may grant floodplain variances, but none that raise the base flood elevation (170-86A(8), 110-29, 110-30)

Riparian buffer: 75 ft from the top of the streambank of a watercourse or the edge of a wetland, where all structures are prohibited, and principal structures stay 25 ft beyond the buffer (170-86C(1)(b), (c), (3)(a)). Development within 100 ft of a stream or of a pond over 1/4 acre needs special exception review (170-86E(4))

Steep slopes: where more than 5,000 sq ft is disturbed, structures on slopes of 15% to 25% are a conditional use and on slopes of 25% or more are prohibited (170-86F(3)(a), (6), (8)). Wetlands: no building may be built or enlarged in a wetland, and a lot needs 75% of its minimum area outside wetlands (170-86B(4), (5))

Nonconforming lot in R-1 or R-2 held alone: a single-family dwelling with any attached permitted accessory use may be built on 3,500 sq ft, 35 ft wide, front 25 ft, rear 15 ft, sides 3 ft and 11 ft together, coverage 50%. An existing single-family dwelling on such a lot 'may be enlarged to comply with, but not exceed' those figures (170-88F(1)(a)[1], [2]). Whether an in-law suite, a special exception use, is a 'permitted accessory use' here is not settled

Accessory buildings: sheds and similar buildings at most 15 ft tall. Detached garages at least 4 ft from the side and rear lines, behind the house's front building line and at most 15 ft tall (170-83H(3)(c), (d)). Two principal buildings on one lot must each meet the rules as if on its own lot (170-89A)

The conditional use G-16 'Lawful use not otherwise permitted' reaches only a use 'that is required to be permitted by the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code' (170-83G(16)). Variances: 170-17, with no bar on a use variance

A dwelling unit is 'One or more rooms, including a kitchen (or kitchenette) and sanitary facilities ... having a separate and independent entrance' (170-23 'Dwelling' A). A suite with its own kitchen reads as a dwelling unit, so it needs its own entrance

Rental: an annual residential rental license, with inspection, is needed for a regulated rental unit (142-8A(1)). Exempt is 'One dwelling unit that is on the same lot as a second dwelling unit, provided the two dwellings are only occupied by the owner and persons who are related to the owner' (142-8A(2)(d)). A suite rented to someone not related to the owner needs the license
Carbonate areas: development there needs a geologist's review of karst features and a Municipal Engineer report, and buildings must be sited to keep sinkhole risk low (170-86G)

Fees: an application that needs a Zoning Hearing Board hearing, such as the in-law suite special exception, is $1,500. A zoning application is $150 and an occupancy permit $100 (170-22A). The change of use needs an occupancy permit (170-12D)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Borough of Wilson Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-17. Read: Article II, Article III (170-23), Articles V, VI and VIII, Article XIII from 170-79 to 170-83F(4) and 170-83G(16), H(3), H(9), 170-86, Article XV, Article XVI, Chapter 110 from 110-1 to 110-27C and code searches. Not read: Article I beyond 170-6, Article IV, Articles VII (H-1), IX (C-1), X (C-2), XI (I-1), XII (PRD overlay), XVII, XVIII (Redevelopment Overlay), 170-83 G except G-16 and H except H-3 and H-9, 170-84, 170-85, 170-87, the PDF attachments (Table of Use Regulations, Table 2 parking) and Chapter 110 after 110-27C (variances, definitions). A code search finds 'H-9 In-law suite' only in R-1, R-2 and TC. Also read: the Chapter 142 rental license rule (142-8) and code search snippets of the two PDF attachments. Open points: whether the accessory dwelling unit definition (800 sq ft, two people, owner occupancy) binds an in-law suite, whether the Board will require relatives, whether the suite counts toward the average lot area per dwelling unit, whether an addition in the floodplain is a new structure or an improvement, and the Table of Use Regulations and Table 2 parking rows, read only as search snippets.

term.note: 'H-9 In-law suite'. The code also defines an 'accessory dwelling unit' (170-23 'Dwelling' H), which no use list names

status.note: Special exception in R-1, R-2 and TC. The stated intent is for related family members, but the section sets no family test

scope_districts.note: A code search finds the in-law suite listed only in R-1, R-2 and TC

status_outside.note: 'no building, structure or land shall be used or occupied except for the purposes permitted in § 170-82' (170-79), and a use marked 'x' in the table is not permitted (170-80D). A code search of the table, a PDF that was not opened, shows the row 'H-9 In-Law Suite SE SE X SE X'. The H-1, C-1, C-2 and I-1 use lists were not read one by one

status_by_form.note: 'No new separate structures on the same lot with the principal residence shall be permitted to be constructed for this use'

path.note: Zoning Hearing Board after a hearing, with a site plan and Planning Commission review (170-10B(2), 170-11, 170-15)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 170-17A(1) to (5). No bar on a use variance

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2)
value.conditions: A detached or semidetached building with not more than two dwelling units, entirely separated by vertical walls or horizontal floors, unpierced except for access to the outside or a common cellar. Lot 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide and 100 ft deep, with 2,500 sq ft per unit. Front and rear 25 ft, side 8 ft and 16 ft for both. Building coverage at most 45%. No family or owner rule

requires.condition: A lot at least 50 ft wide

value.note: A two-unit building, not an in-law suite. The code does not say how an existing house becomes one, so ask the zoning officer. The definition of a two-family detached dwelling names only units stacked over one another (170-23 'Dwelling' E), while the use text allows vertical walls or horizontal floors (170-83B(2))

historic_bypass.note: No historic path was found in the parts read

value.condition: The stated intent of the in-law suite rules is 'to allow for related family members to reside on the premises'. The section sets no family test, but the Board may ask for one.

If the code's accessory dwelling unit definition binds the suite, the unit may have at most three rooms or 800 sq ft of livable area or 40% of the residential floor area, whichever is less, is not meant for more than two people, stays in the same ownership as the house, and the owner must live in the principal unit. The in-law suite section sets its own standards and names no accessory dwelling unit, so this is not settled.

The suite must be registered with the Borough Code Enforcement Officer, and the Northampton County Department of Human Services or another agency must certify that the wastewater facilities can serve the house and the suite.
TC lists no single-family or two-family dwelling. A house there is a nonconforming use, which may be enlarged by no more than 40% of its floor or ground area, with the parking the enlargement needs.

In the floodplain 'All structures, with the exception of those specifically allowed in § 170-86A(4)' are prohibited, and none of those is a dwelling or an addition to one. New construction in the floodway is prohibited. No variance may be granted for a structure the floodplain rules prohibit.

disputed_by.note: An addition may be read as an improvement of an existing structure, which in the FF and FA areas is allowed with full floodproofing at 10% or more of its market value. In the floodway no improvement of an existing structure is allowed (170-86A(6)(a))

value.condition: An accessory structure in the identified floodplain area 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', may have at most 200 sq ft and may have no sanitary facilities. Chapter 110 variances relieve only its elevation and floodproofing rules.

In the floodplain, new construction and substantial improvements are prohibited unless a variance is obtained, and then the lowest floor must be at or above the regulatory flood elevation. Improving an existing structure by 10% or more of its market value needs full floodproofing. In the floodway no improvement or reconstruction of an existing structure is allowed, so a suite inside the house is barred there too.
The riparian buffer is 75 ft from the top of the streambank of a watercourse, and principal structures stay at least 25 ft beyond the buffer. All structures are prohibited in the buffer.

Development within 100 ft of the normal streambank of a river or stream, or of a pond over 1/4 acre, needs special exception review. Within 75 ft of a wetland's edge all structures are prohibited, and no building may be built or enlarged in a wetland.
Where more than 5,000 sq ft of land is disturbed, a structure on a slope of 15% to 25% is a conditional use and on a slope of 25% or more is prohibited.

types_allowed.note: 'In-law suites shall be part of the principal residence or may be contained in the existing accessory structure such as a garage.' An addition is read as part of the residence, and an accessory building attached by a wall or roof is part of the main building (170-23 'Accessory use or structure'). 'Such as a garage' reaches any existing accessory building

types_not_addressed.note: A suite in an existing garage is allowed. Adding a story to a garage is not named, and garages may be at most 15 ft tall

max_share_of_house.note: 'no more than 25% of the total usable floor area of the principal residence, not including any garage'

max_sqft.note: The in-law suite section sets only the 25% share. The accessory dwelling unit definition caps that unit at three rooms or 800 sq ft of livable area or 40% of the residential floor area, whichever is less (170-23 'Dwelling' H(1)). Whether the definition binds an in-law suite is not settled, so its 800 sq ft is not applied

family_only.note: Only an intent statement: 'to allow for related family members to reside on the premises'

occupancy.value: The stated intent is for related family members. If the accessory dwelling unit definition binds the suite, it is not meant for more than two people.

owner_occupancy.note: The in-law suite section has no owner rule. The accessory dwelling unit definition says 'the principal unit shall be occupied by the owner of the structure at all times' (170-23 'Dwelling' H(3)). Whether it binds an in-law suite is not settled

max_adus.note: 'No more than one in-law suite shall be permitted per residential dwelling.'

sale_apart_allowed.note: The in-law suite section says nothing on ownership. The accessory dwelling unit definition keeps the whole structure 'in the same ownership at all times' (170-23 'Dwelling' H(3)). Whether it binds an in-law suite is not settled

max_height_ft.note: 'Garages shall not exceed 15 feet in height.'

value.where: A detached garage which is accessory to a residence, behind the house's front building line
value.note: The suite may use only an existing accessory building, so these yards hold for a garage conversion

spaces_required.note: 'The required off-street parking for the principal dwelling plus one additional off-street parking space for the in-law suite'

min_lot_sqft.note: 6,000 sq ft, 60 ft wide. 'Average lot area per dwelling unit (square feet): 6,000' (170-32B). Whether the suite counts as a dwelling unit for it is not settled, so it is not applied

Single-family detached: 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide. Semidetached 3,000 sq ft, 30 ft wide. 'Average lot area per dwelling unit (square feet): 5,000' for a single-family detached lot and 3,000 for a semidetached one (170-37A(2), B(2)). Whether the suite counts as a dwelling unit for it is not settled, so it is not applied

setback_sides_total_ft.note: Semidetached: one side yard of 8 ft

max_building_coverage.note: 45% for a semidetached or two-family dwelling

min_lot_sqft.note: 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide, 100 ft deep. The average lot area per dwelling unit is left blank
